result.candidate_tests: 97 passed, 1 pre-existing non-failing Starlette deprecation warning

false_failure_investigated_and_explained.what_happened: A first run of START_HERE.py verify reported overall FAIL with seven failures: structured_syntax, package_hygiene, task_dag, sidecar_compose, application_tests, subject_identity and manifest.
causes: Running 07_IMPLEMENTATION/apply/semantic_classify.py from inside the extracted pack wrote 07_IMPLEMENTATION/apply/__pycache__ into the pack itself. That alone produced package_hygiene junk, subject_identity file_count 395 versus actual 396, and a manifest set mismatch naming the .pyc.
The interpreter chosen for that run had neither PyYAML nor pytest, which produced structured_syntax, task_dag and application_tests failures.

sidecar_compose reporting 'cli-tools service missing' was downstream of the same PyYAML absence: the checker could not parse the compose files it was asserting against. It passes once the parser is available, so it was not a real Compose defect.
resolution: Re-extracted the sealed ZIP into a clean directory and verified with the project's own .venv interpreter (PyYAML 6.0.3, pytest 9.1.1): overall PASS, zero failures.
Removed the __pycache__ contamination from the working extraction and re-verified it as well: overall PASS, zero failures.
false_failure_investigated_and_explained.lesson: The pack verifier asserts over its own directory, so running any pack tooling from inside the extraction invalidates its integrity check. Run pack tooling from outside, or re-extract before verifying, and always verify with an interpreter that has PyYAML and pytest.

what_this_does_not_prove: Any product runtime behaviour. This is Task Pack integrity only, and product_runtime_verdict remains NOT_RUN in the pack's own report.
